editorial: Chile was expensive relative to much of our South America trip, especially once Rapa Nui and Patagonia entered the picture.

Some anchors from our notes: a decent Rapa Nui restaurant meal was around USD25, three grocery-based meals for two cost roughly USD22, meals near our Torres del Paine stay were around USD22 each, and an extra night there cost us USD125 versus a listed USD172.
Transport, remote accommodation and park logistics—not Santiago sightseeing—are what stretch the budget.

alternatives.title: What if we had a bigger budget?
editorial: We'd spend it on Patagonia logistics: strategically located accommodation, a better-supported car rental and the right refugio setup for the Base Torres hike. Rapa Nui would also justify a nicer stay simply because we wanted to linger.

alternatives.title: What if we had a smaller budget?
editorial: Choose either Rapa Nui or Patagonia rather than both. They are each expensive detours from Santiago, and trying to economise while doing every remote region can make the trip feel like a series of compromises.

title: What it's Going to Cost
